content.title: Aeva shares soar after deal with European automaker
content.summary: Shares of Aeva Technologies, a Silicon Valley-based maker of lidar units that ​help autonomous vehicles sense their surroundings, rose more than 18% ‌in midday trading on Wednesday after the company announced an exclusive deal to supply ‌a European maker of passenger vehicles.  Aeva did not name the automaker, but analysts at Morgan Stanley and Canaccord Genuity last month said in research notes they believe the customer is Mercedes-Benz.  Aeva said in a press ⁠release the automaker will ‌use its sensors, which can generate a 3D map of the world around a vehicle as well as ‍detect how fast objects such as pedestrians are moving, for autonomous-driving functions in all of the automaker's combustion, electric and hybrid vehicles outside of China.

content.title: The Week in Numbers: Nvidia marches on, Formula One zooms
content.summary:
STORY: From Nvidia's fortunes easing AI bubble fears to a new investor for the Mercedes Formula One team.

This is the Week in Numbers

:: Week in Numbers

:: $65 billion

$65 billion is how much Nvidia expects for its fiscal fourth-quarter sales.

The world's most valuable company also announced third-quarter sales rose 62%, their first acceleration in seven quarters. 

Global markets have looked to the chip designer to see whether investing billions of dollars in AI infrastructure expansion has resulted in an AI bubble.

:: $135 billion

A $135 billion economic stimulus package was approved by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's cabinet.

It marks the first major policy initiative under the new leader, who has pledged to pursue expansionary fiscal measures.

It's also Tokyo's largest stimulus since the pandemic.

:: 81%

Xiaomi reported a near 81% jump in third-quarter profit.

It comes with the Chinese tech giant moving further towards electric vehicles.

Xiaomi is also the world's third-largest smartphone maker.

It said the quarterly growth was driven by EVs, AI and other new projects.

:: $82,000

Bitcoin fell to around $82,000 on Friday, falling to its lowest level in more than six months.

The decline comes amid a broad sell-off in riskier assets.

One analyst recently told Reuters that because cryptocurrencies generally move with the stock market, they haven't become an asset of alternative value to hedge against fear in other sectors.

:: 15%

A 15% stake in the Mercedes Formula One team is how much CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz now owns.

It comes out of the one-third stake held by principal Toto Wolff.

No financial details were given for the personal acquisition but media reports last week said the deal valued the former champions at a record $6 billion.

content.title: CrowdStrike founder Kurtz buys into Mercedes F1 team
content.summary:
STORY: CrowdStrike founder and chief executive George Kurtz has bought into the Mercedes Formula One team.

Kurtz is taking 15% of the one-third stake held by principal Toto Wolff, both parties announced on Thursday.

No financial details were given for the personal acquisition but media reports last week said the deal valued the former champions at a record $6 billion.

Wolff, Mercedes-Benz and Jim Ratcliffe's petrochemicals giant Ineos each hold one-third stakes and the governance and leadership of the team will not be affected by the deal.

Kurtz will become the team's technology adviser and joins the strategic steering committee alongside Wolff, Ratcliffe and Mercedes-Benz chairman Ola Kaellenius.

In an interview with reporters, Kurtz said he sees a great opportunity to grow the sport, particularly in the U.S. market.

He said he had total alignment with Wolff, subscribed to his leadership style and had been discussing taking a stake for several years.

He ruled out one day taking on a greater role in the team, saying his focus remains with Cybersecurity company CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike has been a team partner since 2019 with branding on the car and apparel.

Mercedes won eight constructors' titles in a row from 2014 to 2021, and are currently second overall behind champions McLaren, who also use the German manufacturer's engines.
